name: Prefix caching and PagedAttention block sharing: granularity of sharing and the 128K cache miss penalty
arithmetic_intensity: In standard PagedAttention (SOSP'23, arXiv:2309.06180, [[sched-vllm-pagedattention-sosp23]]), KV cache memory is allocated in non-contiguous physical blocks of fixed size B (typically 16 tokens). Within a single request using parallel sampling or beam search, all prompt tokens and shared prefix branches share physical blocks via reference counting; newly sampled tokens diverge using block-level Copy-on-Write (CoW). Across distinct requests, sharing requires Automatic Prefix Caching (vLLM APC, [[flop-pagedattention-vllm]]) or RadixAttention (SGLang, arXiv:2312.07104, [[flop-sglang]]). WHAT IS SHARED: Full completed token blocks whose token IDs and system state hash match existing nodes in the radix/hash tree (system prompts, few-shot examples, multi-turn history). WHAT IS NOT SHARED: (1) Partial blocks at sequence tails: tokens beyond the last 16-token boundary cannot be indexed into the shared radix tree until full, requiring local recomputation; (2) Request-specific states: position embeddings when not rotary/relative, adapter weights (unless explicitly keyed), sampling configurations, and layer activations; (3) Cross-tenant blocks across non-identical hardware or divergent numerical backends. THE 128K CACHE MISS PENALTY: When a 128K shared prefix hits in cache, prefill attention FLOPs drop from O(L^2) to O(t_new * L), avoiding 2 * n_heads * head_dim * L^2 operations (for Llama-3.1-70B with 64 Q heads, head_dim 128, L=131,072: avoiding ~35.2 TFLOPs of attention per request). When memory pressure evicts a 128K prefix block, a subsequent request suffers a complete cache miss. This inverts the execution profile from a sub-second memory-bound token generation into a compute-bound 128K prefill, driving TTFT from tens of milliseconds to dozens of seconds and stalling the scheduler.
scales_with: block_size B (typically 16; smaller blocks reduce internal fragmentation waste to <4% but increase radix tree overhead and kernel indirection)
prefix_hit_rate (governs the probability of paying the O(L^2) recomputation penalty)
eviction_policy (LRU eviction under KV pressure triggers catastrophic recomputation cliffs for long prefixes)
prefix_length L (the penalty of a miss scales quadratically with L in attention flops)
workarounds: Pin shared system prompts and high-frequency long-context prefixes in HBM to prevent LRU eviction cascades
Align prompts to the 16-token block boundary so the maximum possible prefix length is shared across requests
Offload evicted prefix blocks to host DRAM (via Mooncake or LMCache) rather than discarding them, converting an O(L^2) compute recomputation into a PCIe/CXL bandwidth transfer
notes: EMPIRICAL SHARING AND FRAGMENTATION MEASUREMENTS: In the PagedAttention paper (arXiv:2309.06180, [[sched-vllm-pagedattention-sosp23]]), prior contiguous memory management wasted 60-80% of KV cache memory due to internal fragmentation (pre-allocating max context lengths) and external fragmentation. PagedAttention reduced memory waste to under 4%, improving throughput by 2x-4x across basic sampling and parallel decoding. In SGLang's RadixAttention evaluation (arXiv:2312.07104, [[flop-sglang]]), automatic prefix reuse achieved up to 6.4x higher serving throughput on multi-turn chat, few-shot benchmarks, and agent tree-search workloads. VERIFIED NEGATIVE AT 128K: Neither SOSP'23 vLLM nor the original SGLang paper published prefix caching hit/miss benchmarks at 128K context (vLLM evaluated max 2048-token sequences on A100; SGLang evaluated up to 4K-8K sequences). The cost of a 128K miss in production is derived from the quadratic attention prefill scaling and the capacity cliff when 128K prefixes compete with concurrent batch slots.
